name.description: The name of the Cloud Bigtable instance.
name.rationale: Human-chosen resource name for Terraform/API; it is not a cryptographic material and does not enumerate who may access data.

cluster.description: A cluster for the instance. At least one cluster must exist when the instance is created; you can add up to 8 clusters within 8 regions. Removing this block makes the provider default to backend values.
cluster.rationale: A structural block in HCL, not a secret. Security-sensitive values (for example `kms_key_name` or `zone`) live on nested attributes and are assessed there, not on the fact that a `cluster` block exists.

cluster_id.description: The unique identifier for the cluster within the instance.
cluster_id.rationale: Distinguishes one cluster from another in config; the string is not a principal identifier and does not open network access by itself.

zone.description: The zone to serve this cluster in. If unspecified, the provider zone is used. Each cluster must use a different zone in the same region.
zone.rationale: Zone determines physical location and data residency; policies may whitelist approved regions/zones (`cluster.zone`).

num_nodes.description: The number of nodes in the cluster. If unset and autoscaling is not configured, Bigtable sizes nodes from data footprint.
num_nodes.rationale: Performance/capacity tuning only; node count does not list IAM members or contain keys.

autoscaling_config.description: Optional autoscaling configuration for the cluster. Only one of `autoscaling_config` or `num_nodes` should be set.
autoscaling_config.rationale: Container for autoscaling parameters; the block label is not sensitive—only the nested min/max and targets affect operations, not identity or encryption root of trust.

min_nodes.description: Minimum number of nodes for autoscaling.
min_nodes.rationale: Sets a capacity floor for autoscaling; it does not define who can read or write Bigtable data.

max_nodes.description: Maximum number of nodes for autoscaling.
max_nodes.rationale: Sets a capacity ceiling; unrelated to IAM bindings and not a secret.

cpu_target.rationale: Operational tuning target for scaling behavior only; does not authenticate clients.

storage_target.rationale: Another scaling signal for capacity planning; not an authorization mechanism.

storage_type.description: The storage type for the cluster: `SSD` (default) or `HDD`.
storage_type.rationale: Chooses media class for performance/cost; both options still rely on platform-managed encryption at rest and do not control IAM.

kms_key_name.description: Fully qualified name of the Cloud KMS key for CMEK (customer-managed encryption) for this cluster.
kms_key_name.rationale: CMEK ties encryption at rest to your KMS key; policies often require a non-empty key in an approved project/region (`cluster.kms_key_name`).

node_scaling_factor.description: Optional scaling factor for node granularity for this cluster.
node_scaling_factor.rationale: Provider-internal sizing hint; unrelated to secrets, principals, or encryption keys.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Public, non-secret project identifier used for API routing; it does not prove caller identity.

instance_type.description: DEVELOPMENT or PRODUCTION (Google is unifying these; prefer PRODUCTION for new instances).
instance_type.rationale: Changes sizing/quota characteristics only; it neither publishes data nor adds IAM grants.

display_name.description: Human-readable display name for the instance in consoles.
display_name.rationale: Console label only; does not alter IAM, keys, or network ACLs.

force_destroy.description: When true, Terraform can destroy the instance even when that would normally be blocked.
force_destroy.rationale: IaC-only destroy behavior; not a data-exposure toggle, though enabling careless destroys can harm availability—still distinct from granting anonymous reads.

deletion_protection.description: When true (or unset in state per provider behavior), Terraform apply/destroy that would delete the instance fails.
deletion_protection.rationale: Blocks accidental destructive changes to the instance and its data plane availability.

labels.description: Non-authoritative labels applied via Terraform; see `effective_labels` for the full set in GCP.
labels.rationale: Key/value tags for governance and billing; label pairs are not secrets and labeling alone does not authenticate requests.

tags.description: Resource tags (key/value) per GCP tag requirements.
tags.rationale: Organizational tags for policy/cost tracking; not credential material.

terraform_labels.description: Labels from Terraform configuration merged with provider default labels.
terraform_labels.rationale: Derived labels for state/plan output; read-only convenience field, not an access grant.

effective_labels.description: All labels present on the resource in GCP, including Terraform, API, and service-managed labels.
effective_labels.rationale: Aggregated label snapshot from GCP; informational only and does not replace IAM decisions.
